name: Wankhede Stadium
pitchType: Red soil with true bounce, carry & pace; evening sea breeze assists swing
historicMoment: Hosted 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup Final; MS Dhoni struck the match-winning six.

name: Lord's Cricket Ground
pitchType: Famous 8-foot (2.5m) natural slope running south-to-north; true bounce & swing
historicMoment: Known as the 'Home of Cricket'; hosted 2019 World Cup Final with the Super Over finish.

name: Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG)
pitchType: Drop-in pitch offering even bounce and pace; colossal boundary dimensions
historicMoment: Hosted the first-ever Test match in 1877; 1992 and 2015 ICC World Cup Finals.

name: Eden Gardens
pitchType: Good batting track with reliable bounce; aids orthodox spinners as match progresses
historicMoment: VVS Laxman's 281 in 2001 vs Australia; Rohit Sharma's world record 264 in 2014.

name: The Oval (Kia Oval)
pitchType: Traditionally one of the fastest, bounciest pitches in England with exceptional carry
historicMoment: Birthplace of The Ashes in 1882; traditionally hosts the final Test of the English summer.

name: Sydney Cricket Ground (SCG)
pitchType: Historic bulli soil providing classic turn for spinners from Day 3 onwards
historicMoment: Traditional New Year's Pink Test; famous heritage Members Pavilion and clock tower.

name: Narendra Modi Stadium
pitchType: Features both red-soil and black-soil wickets; expansive 63-acre complex
historicMoment: Largest cricket stadium in the world; hosted the 2023 ICC World Cup Final.

name: HPCA Stadium
pitchType: High altitude (1,457m) Ryegrass outfield; brisk chill aids extra pace and lateral swing
historicMoment: Set against the dramatic snow-capped Dhauladhar mountain range in Himachal Pradesh.

name: Newlands Cricket Ground
pitchType: Seamer-friendly conditions on opening days; takes spin later under Mediterranean sun
historicMoment: Overlooked by the majestic Table Mountain and Devil's Peak; iconic Test venue.

name: Kensington Oval
pitchType: Hard, true bounce and fast outfield; Mecca of West Indian cricket heritage
historicMoment: Hosted the 2007 ICC World Cup Final and the 2024 ICC T20 World Cup Final.

name: M. Chinnaswamy Stadium
pitchType: Flat batting paradise with short boundaries (60m square) and high-altitude thin air
historicMoment: Chris Gayle's record 175* off 66 balls in IPL 2013; first stadium in world to use solar power.

name: M. A. Chidambaram Stadium (Chepauk)
pitchType: Dry clay surface offering intense spin and low bounce; humid coastal air
historicMoment: Historic Tied Test between India and Australia in 1986; yellow fortress of CSK.

name: Trent Bridge
pitchType: Pungent heavy atmosphere encourages heavy swing; ultra-fast outfield and high scoring
historicMoment: Venue of England's world record 481/6 vs Australia; Stuart Broad 8/15 in 2015 Ashes.

name: Adelaide Oval
pitchType: Famous drop-in pitch with very short square boundaries and lengthy straight boundaries
historicMoment: Hosted the first-ever Day/Night pink-ball Test match in cricket history (2015).

name: Gaddafi Stadium
pitchType: Classic subcontinent surface; flat early with reverse swing emerging later
historicMoment: Hosted the 1996 Cricket World Cup Final where Sri Lanka lifted their maiden title.

name: Galle International Stadium
pitchType: Coastal breezes off Indian Ocean aid seam early, turning into an explosive spin minefield
historicMoment: Bordered on two sides by the Indian Ocean and the 17th-century UNESCO Dutch Fort.

name: Dubai International Stadium
pitchType: Fair contest between bat and ball; renowned for evening dew factor
historicMoment: Distinguished by its circular 'Ring of Fire' roof lighting system of 350 floodlights.

name: Old Trafford
pitchType: Quickest and bounciest pitch in England; retains reverse swing and spin late in Tests
historicMoment: Shane Warne bowled the 'Ball of the Century' to Mike Gatting here in the 1993 Ashes.

name: SuperSport Park
pitchType: High-altitude fast track with sharp steepling bounce and rapid outfield
historicMoment: Fortress for South African fast bowling with picturesque open grass banks.

name: Edgbaston Cricket Ground
pitchType: Lively pace and reliable bounce; famous for vibrant, vocal Eric Hollies Stand atmosphere
historicMoment: Site of the dramatic 2005 Ashes Test thriller where England won by just 2 runs.

name: The Gabba (Brisbane Cricket Ground)
pitchType: Hard, fast, and bouncy surface with true carry; renowned as the fastest pitch in Australia
historicMoment: Site of the first-ever Tied Test in 1960 and India's famous 2021 fortress breach.

name: Headingley Cricket Ground
pitchType: Traditionally aids swing and seam under Yorkshire cloud cover; reliable batting track on dry days
historicMoment: Host to Botham's Miracle Ashes Test in 1981 and Ben Stokes' 135* miraculous 1-wicket heist in 2019.
homeTeam: Yorkshire County Cricket Club & Northern Superchargers

name: Imperial Wanderers Stadium (The Bullring)
pitchType: High altitude (1753m) allows ball to travel farther; fiery pace and steep, uncomfortable bounce
historicMoment: Venue of the iconic 438 ODI chase in 2006 and the inaugural 2007 ICC World Twenty20 Final.

name: Kingsmead Cricket Ground
pitchType: Coastal humidity produces sharp late seam; tide movements historically influence moisture
historicMoment: Hosted the Timeless Test of 1939 and Yuvraj Singh's famous 6 sixes in an over in 2007.

name: National Bank Stadium
pitchType: Historically a fortress for spin and reverse swing; true batting surface in first two days
historicMoment: Pakistan remained undefeated in Test matches here for 45 consecutive years from 1955 to 2000.

name: Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium
pitchType: High-scoring batting paradise with consistent bounce and brisk outfield
historicMoment: Home to Rahul Dravid's epic 270 in 2004 and Shoaib Akhtar's searing home-town spells.

name: R. Premadasa International Stadium
pitchType: Slow, turning track offering prodigal grip for spinners; high humidity brings evening dew
historicMoment: Hosted the 2012 ICC World Twenty20 Final and Sri Lanka's record 952/6 against India in 1997.

name: Sinhalese Sports Club (SSC) Ground
pitchType: Sri Lanka's premier Test ground with traditional good carry on morning one, turning sharply by Day 4
historicMoment: Venue of Kumar Sangakkara and Mahela Jayawardene's world record 624-run partnership in 2006.

name: Basin Reserve
pitchType: Classic grassy green seaming pitch; famous Wellington cross-winds heavily assist swing bowling
historicMoment: New Zealand defeated England by 1 run following on in 2023, only the second such finish in Test history.

name: Eden Park
pitchType: Unique baseball/rugby hybrid dimensions with notoriously short straight boundaries and huge square boundaries
historicMoment: Grant Elliott struck Dale Steyn for a penultimate-ball six to send New Zealand into their first World Cup Final in 2015.

name: Hagley Oval
pitchType: True bounce with lush grassy embankment; Brendon McCullum smashed the fastest Test century (54 balls) here in 2016.
historicMoment: Venue for Brendon McCullum's farewell 54-ball century and the 2022 Women's Cricket World Cup Final.

name: Seddon Park
pitchType: Boutique circular ground with lush green turf; known for high-scoring ODIs and swing in overcast conditions
historicMoment: Regular fortress for New Zealand Test series wins with its distinctive grassy bank ambiance.

name: Sharjah Cricket Stadium
pitchType: Flat, dry surface with short boundaries, renowned for high six-counts and low bounce in second innings
historicMoment: Host to Sachin Tendulkar's legendary 'Desert Storm' in 1998 and Javed Miandad's last-ball six in 1986.

name: Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium
pitchType: Large outfield dimensions with dry, abrasive pitch; demands athletic running between wickets
historicMoment: Hosted numerous Pakistan home Test triumphs and the 2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup semi-finals.

name: Sabina Park
pitchType: Picturesque backdrop of the Blue Mountains; historically fast and fiery, now offering balanced contest
historicMoment: Sir Garfield Sobers scored his record 365* here in 1958; Brian Lara scored 375 against England in 1994.

name: Queen's Park Oval
pitchType: Spin-friendly clay that dries out under the Caribbean sun; legendary carnival atmosphere
historicMoment: India chased down a then-record 403 in the 4th innings in 1976 led by Gavaskar and Viswanath.
homeTeam: Trinidad & Tobago Red Force & Trinbago Knight Riders

name: Daren Sammy Cricket Ground
pitchType: Good true bounce with Atlantic trade winds assisting seamers and power-hitters over deep midwicket
historicMoment: First international venue in the Caribbean named after an active player; hosted 2010 T20 World Cup.

name: Providence Stadium
pitchType: Low and slow coastal clay surface; paradise for finger spinners and cutters
historicMoment: Lasith Malinga took 4 wickets in 4 balls against South Africa in the 2007 Cricket World Cup here.

name: Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium
pitchType: Flat, hard track with true carry; renowned for high-octane 250+ IPL T20 encounters
historicMoment: Hosted the IPL Finals in 2017 and 2019, both thrilling 1-run finishes won by Mumbai Indians.

name: BRSABV Ekana Cricket Stadium
pitchType: Dual black-soil and red-soil pitches offering either gripping turn or good pace; huge boundary sizes
historicMoment: Rohit Sharma struck 111* off 61 balls against West Indies in the venue's inaugural T20I in 2018.

name: Arun Jaitley Stadium (Feroz Shah Kotla)
pitchType: Compact boundaries with low bounce; transformed recently into a high-scoring batting track in T20s
historicMoment: Anil Kumble took a historic 10 wickets in an innings (10/74) against Pakistan here in 1999.

name: Holkar Stadium
pitchType: High-scoring batting paradise with compact boundaries and lightning outfield
historicMoment: Virender Sehwag smashed 219 against West Indies in 2011, then the highest individual ODI score.

name: Niranjan Shah Stadium (SCA Stadium)
pitchType: Flat, hard batting wicket known for mammoth first-innings totals and true bounce
historicMoment: Host to Yashasvi Jaiswal's unbeaten 214* with 12 sixes against England in the 2024 Test series.

name: Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Stadium
pitchType: Lush green coastal venue offering consistent bounce and heavy six-hitting conditions
historicMoment: MS Dhoni scored his breakout maiden ODI century (148 off 123) against Pakistan here in 2005.

name: Green Park Stadium
pitchType: Traditional low-bounce subcontinent surface heavily assisting reverse swing and orthodox spin
historicMoment: Hosted India's historic 500th Test match in 2016 against New Zealand.
